title: Our repos and how a ticket is written
bridge: Our repos are like the workspaces of one big project: each has its own job, tools and owners. Except: they are separate GitHub repos. A change that spans two needs two PRs, and an agent's token covers exactly one repo.
intro: Every ticket names files in one of our repos, so you need to know which repo holds what. This lesson walks through the repos the platform touches. Then it shows how a ticket is written, so you can read any of the 242 the same way.

picture.caption: The repos the platform touches, and how they connect.

steps.text: Byte's broker code becomes the base of the ai-agents broker
its services are deployed as Terraform helm_release units in infrastructure
Nova and the routines open PRs in fcp, one repo per token
fcp's CI publishes new versions; gitops deploys them to product clusters
skills that people and agents load when they work in fcp
the agents' kb_search tool reads the brain pages

p: fcp holds the product. cloud/ is the Django backend and client/ the on-prem client. sdk/ is the Python SDK, frontend/ the dashboard you know, and common/ the shared code. Agents work in this repo; the platform does not live here.

CI lives in .github/workflows. cloud-ci, client-ci and sdk-ci run on every push to any branch. frontend-ci runs on pull requests to main. Most jobs run on fcp-runner-set, our own GitHub Actions runners.

A PR title looks like [FE] RH-6589: Inline the session icon, with the Jira key from project RH. The PR template has four parts: Summary of Changes, Implementation Details, Testing Performed, References. fcp has no CODEOWNERS file: any engineer may review any area.

infrastructure holds the cloud: OpenTofu (the open-source Terraform) with Terragrunt. The old tree is multi_tenant/accounts/<account>/..., the new tree is terraform/accounts/<account>/<cloud>/<region>/<component>. It also holds modules/, the Packer images and Vault's setup. Only DevOps can approve here: its CODEOWNERS is @RhinoHealth/devops.

Internal tools run on inf-rhinohealth, a Kubernetes cluster in the infrastructure account. They are deployed as Terraform helm_release units in this repo, like n8n. The gateway, broker, orchestrator and Slack app will be too.
gitops holds Argo CD apps and Helm charts for the product clusters only. No Argo app targets inf-rhinohealth, so our agent services never go through gitops.

callout.text: Agents never apply, destroy, sync or dispatch. A person runs terraform plan and apply in infrastructure and syncs in gitops, always.

p: byte is our PR review agent, maintained mostly by Nave. It is TypeScript with a broker, src/broker.ts, that already passed a security review. That broker becomes the start of ours.

ai-agents is the new platform repo, created in G3-01. It is TypeScript on Node 24 with npm workspaces, one folder per service, plus folders that hold only data. Only evals/ is Python, because the bench runner is Python.

claude-plugins is the new private plugin marketplace from G8. It holds rhino-core, fe-guild and be-guild plugins: skills and hooks for people and agents. The public agent-skills repo is for customers and is not ours to use for this.
sections.because: We read the ai-agents layout once, because every platform ticket names a file in one of these folders.

code.text:
ai-agents/
├── package.json        npm workspaces; "type": "module"; Node >=24
├── shared/             zod schemas and types, config, small Jira/Slack/GitHub clients
├── gateway/            LLM gateway (G0)
├── broker/             broker, started from Byte's src/broker.ts (G3)
├── orchestrator/       Temporal worker: workflows, activities, triggers, routines
├── harness/            nova-worker, runs inside each VM (G3, G4, G5)
│   ├── workflows/      *.js scripts for the Workflow tool
│   └── prompts/        *.md prompts for judges and subagents
├── slack-app/          Bolt in Socket Mode
├── checks/             required checks: independent approval, locked checks
├── metrics/            nightly delivery metrics (G1)
├── drills/             failure drill kit (G3)
├── routines/           DATA only: charters/*.yaml
├── settings/           DATA: managed-settings.d/*.json, protected-paths.yaml
├── inventory/          DATA: agents.yaml
├── config/             DATA: repos/<repo>.yaml, people.yaml
├── evals/              PYTHON (uv): bench adapters, benches, reports
└── .github/workflows/  ci.yml, images.yml, release-harness.yml

notes.text: One root package.json and one lockfile for every TypeScript package (lesson p1-1).
Code every service imports. The zod schemas live here (lesson p1-5).
Each service folder becomes one Docker image (lesson p1-8).
The harness is not an image: it ships as one bundled file (lesson p1-7).
DATA folders hold YAML and JSON, never code. Code that reads them lives in a service folder.
The one Python corner, with its own uv project.

p: rnd-kb holds the brain's pages and DATA-SCOPE.md, the rules from Security about what may go in. rnd-kb-tooling holds the code: the page linter, the ingest job, the kb search tool and the Slack bot. Shai's kb_tools in that repo is Python, so the brain's tooling stays Python.
Both repos were created on 11 October as empty scaffolds. G6 fills them.

Every ticket uses our Jira format: What, Why, How, plus a code sketch. There are no acceptance criteria and no 'done when' list. How gives practical steps: files, commands, settings and who to talk to.
The title starts with the owning team in brackets, then says what the ticket delivers, in at most about 75 characters. Here is a real ticket with its How steps shortened.
sections.because: We read one ticket field by field, because every ticket has the same shape and you will read hundreds of them.

code.text:
{
  "key": "G0-08",
  "title": "[DevOps] Create the rhino-ai-agents GitHub App, key in Vault, no bypass",
  "team": ["devops", "plat"],
  "days": 1,
  "w": [2, 2],
  "flag": null,
  "deps": ["G0-02"],
  "needs": "G3 broker (W3–5) is the only service that reads the key",
  "what": "Create the private GitHub App rhino-ai-agents that every AI agent pushes and opens PRs with, install it on fcp only, and keep its private key in Vault.",
  "why": "Agents need their own identity so GitHub can tell their work apart and the rules can treat it differently. Installation tokens last 1 hour and can be limited to one repo.",
  "how": [
    "Create the App under RhinoHealth with the settings in the sketch …",
    "Keep the webhook off. …",
    "Install it on RhinoHealth/fcp only (Only select repositories). …",
    "Store app_id and the private key at kvv2 infrastructure/ai-agents/github-app …",
    "Check that the App is not in the fcp ruleset's bypass_actors …"
  ],
  "code": { "file": "ai-agents/settings/github-app.json", "lang": "json", "text": "…" }
}

notes.text: [Team] then an imperative: you know what it delivers from the title alone.
What another goal must provide, or who relies on this one. Here: only the G3 broker reads the key.
What: one or two sentences on what gets built or decided.
Why: what breaks or stays slow without it. This is what you say when someone asks.
How: the steps, with real paths and names. Each full step says exactly what to click or run.
The code sketch: the key file, written with real APIs. Decision tickets have code: null.

p: A sketch shows the shape of the key file: real library calls, real paths, 6 to 35 lines. It is not finished code. Comments in it mark open questions, such as 'check the docs for X' or 'decide with G3'.
When a sketch and the library's docs disagree, the docs win, and you write the difference in the PR. When a comment says decide, you ask the named owner before you build.
sections.because: We read the sketch after What, Why and How, because the sketch is the How written as a file.

code.text:
{
  "name": "rhino-ai-agents",
  "description": "Identity for Rhino's AI agents (Nova and the routines). The broker mints a 1-hour token per run for one repo.",
  "url": "https://github.com/RhinoHealth/ai-agents",
  "public": false,
  "hook_attributes": { "active": false },
  "default_events": [],
  "default_permissions": {
    "metadata": "read",
    "contents": "write",
    "pull_requests": "write",
    "checks": "read",
    "actions": "read"
  }
}

notes.text: A private App: only RhinoHealth can install it.
No webhook. Agent triggers come from Jira polling, Slack and small Actions, so nothing on the internet calls us.
Write access to code, so the broker can push the agent's branch.
Open and update PRs. Approve and merge are refused by the broker and the ruleset.
Read only. There is no workflows permission at all, so GitHub refuses any push from the App that changes .github/workflows.

p: In fcp, agent already means something else: the Rhino Client VMs, such as rhino-agent-qa-1 and the rhinoAgent app. So everything AI is called ai-agents: the AWS account, the repo, the Temporal namespace, the GitHub App rhino-ai-agents and the image ai-agent-sandbox.

In ai-agents, file names are kebab-case, such as ticket-to-pr.ts and git-proxy.ts. Python code keeps snake_case. Environment variables, HTTP paths, JSON fields on the wire and YAML keys never change name, because other tickets rely on them.

lab.faded: Print ticket G3-07 the same way: its title, its number of How steps and its code file. Left to you: change the goal file and the key in the command. Then say in one sentence each what its What, Why, How and code are about.
lab.alone: Write a ticket in our format for a small frontend change you know well. Use a [FE] title under 75 characters and a What of one or two sentences. Add a Why, three to five How steps with real paths, and a 6 to 15 line sketch. No acceptance criteria. Ask a teammate whether they could start from it without asking you anything.
lab.done: You can say which repo holds a given file, and you can read any ticket as What, Why, How and code.

quiz.q: Where will the Helm release that runs the Nova broker live?

options.text: In gitops, as an Argo CD app
options.why: gitops deploys the product clusters only; no Argo app targets inf-rhinohealth.

options.text: In ai-agents, next to the broker's code
options.why: The code and its image are built there, but deploys live in infrastructure.

options.text: In infrastructure, as a Terraform helm_release unit, like n8n
options.why: Internal tools on inf-rhinohealth are deployed from the infrastructure repo.

quiz.q: A ticket's How says: 'Decide with G3: how sandbox VMs reach this.' What do you do?

options.text: Ask the named owner, record the decision in the ticket, then build
options.why: Comments and steps that say decide mark open questions; the owner answers them.

options.text: Pick the option that is quickest to build and note it in the PR
options.why: The choice affects other goals; it is not yours to make alone.

options.text: Add acceptance criteria so the reviewer knows what to check
options.why: Our tickets have no acceptance criteria; open questions are settled with the owner.

quiz.q: Which of these is a well-formed ticket title?

options.why: Nobody knows what it delivers or who owns it.

options.text: Nova should be able to push its branch safely without holding a token in the VM
options.why: Too long, no team, and it describes a wish instead of a deliverable.

options.text: [Platform] Broker: git proxy that checks repo and branch before pushing
options.why: Team in brackets, an imperative deliverable, under 75 characters.

Argo CD apps and Helm charts for the product clusters only.
The new TypeScript platform repo: gateway, broker, orchestrator, harness, Slack app, checks.
The new private plugin marketplace with our skills and hooks.
